question: Why is the sky blue?
poem:
Sunlight holds every color, it is true,
But air scatters most the shorter blue;
That light comes to us from every side,
And paints the sky so blue and wide.

question: What is the capital of France?
poem:
Ask about France and its capital's name,
And Paris is the answer, city of fame;
It sits on the Seine, that river so fair,
With the Eiffel Tower rising in the air.

question: How do plants make their food?
poem:
Green leaves catch the sunlight every day,
And draw in carbon dioxide on the way;
With water from roots, they make sugar to eat,
And release oxygen, a wonderful feat.

question: Why do we have seasons?
poem:
Earth's axis leans as it circles the sun,
So seasons change as the year is run;
The half tipped near has summer's light,
The half tipped far has winter's night.

question: How can I sleep better at night?
poem:
Go to bed at the same time each night,
And put away screens with their bright blue light;
Keep your room dark, cool, and still,
And skip late coffee, if you will.

question: Who wrote Romeo and Juliet?
poem:
William Shakespeare wrote this tragic play,
Of a love that still moves us to this day;
Two young hearts from houses at war,
Meet in Verona and love evermore.

question: What causes thunder?
poem:
Lightning heats the air in a sudden flash,
The air expands fast with a mighty crash;
That shock wave travels through cloud and rain,
And reaches your ears as thunder's refrain.

question: How does a vaccine work?
poem:
A vaccine shows your body a harmless sign,
Of a germ it may meet further down the line;
Your defenses learn and remember its face,
So they act fast if it enters the place.

question: What is the largest planet in our solar system?
poem:
Jupiter is the largest of them all,
It makes every other planet look small;
A giant of gas with a great red storm,
Its clouds swirl on in a striped form.

question: How can I save money each month?
poem:
Write down all the money you spend,
And set a budget from start to end;
Move some to savings when you get paid,
And watch the progress that you have made.

question: Why do leaves change color in autumn?
poem:
As autumn days grow short and cool,
Trees stop making green chlorophyll as a rule;
The yellow and orange hidden inside,
Now show their colors far and wide.

question: How do bees make honey?
poem:
Bees gather nectar from flowers in bloom,
And bring it back home to a waxy room;
They fan it with wings so the water will go,
Then seal it in wax for when cold winds blow.

question: What is the boiling point of water?
poem:
When water is heated at sea level, you see,
It boils at one hundred Celsius degree;
High on a mountain it boils at less heat,
Since the air pressure there is easier to beat.

question: Why do we need to drink water?
poem:
Our bodies are mostly water inside,
It carries our nutrients far and wide;
It cools us with sweat when we get too hot,
So drink through the day, whether thirsty or not.

question: What is the tallest mountain on Earth?
poem:
Mount Everest stands as the tallest peak,
The summit that many brave climbers seek;
On Nepal and China's border it rises high,
Nearly nine kilometers into the sky.

question: How many continents are there?
poem:
Seven continents cover the land on Earth,
Each one of a different shape and worth;
Asia, Africa, and the Americas two,
With Europe, Australia, and Antarctica too.

question: Why is the ocean salty?
poem:
Rain slowly wears away rocks on land,
And rivers bring minerals down to the strand;
In the sea the water evaporates away,
But all of the salt is left there to stay.

question: What do giant pandas eat?
poem:
Giant pandas eat bamboo leaves, stems, and shoots,
And sometimes small animals, eggs, or fruits;
They chew for twelve hours or more every day,
To get enough energy to live and to play.

question: How does the heart work?
poem:
Your heart is a muscle that pumps every beat,
It pushes your blood from your head to your feet;
Through arteries, oxygen travels in blood,
Then veins bring it back in a steady flood.

question: Why do we yawn?
poem:
No one knows fully why we yawn each day,
But scientists have some ideas to say;
It may cool the brain when it gets too warm,
And seeing a yawn makes others conform.

question: What is gravity?
poem:
Gravity is a force that pulls things down,
It keeps our feet on the ground in every town;
It holds the Moon close as it circles our Earth,
And keeps Earth around the Sun since its birth.

question: Who painted the Mona Lisa?
poem:
Leonardo da Vinci painted her smile,
In Italy, working on it a long while;
Today in the Louvre in Paris she stays,
Where millions of visitors come to gaze.

question: When did humans first land on the Moon?
poem:
In nineteen sixty-nine, in July,
Apollo Eleven flew up to the sky;
Neil Armstrong stepped out on the lunar ground,
The first human there, as the world gathered round.

question: Who was Napoleon Bonaparte?
poem:
Napoleon Bonaparte led France long ago,
A general who became emperor, you know;
He won many battles across Europe's land,
Till Waterloo ended the power he planned.

question: How does the internet work?
poem:
The internet joins computers far and wide,
Through cables and signals on every side;
Your data is split into packets so small,
Then joined back together, delivering it all.

question: What is a black hole?
poem:
A black hole forms when a huge star collapses tight,
Its gravity grows so strong it traps even light;
Nothing that crosses its edge can get out,
That is what makes it so dark, without doubt.

question: Why do we need sleep?
poem:
Sleep lets your body repair and rest,
So you can wake up and feel your best;
Your brain sorts the memories made in the day,
And clears out the waste that gets in its way.

question: How can I reduce stress?
poem:
Take a slow breath and walk outside,
Move your body and let worries subside;
Talk to a friend and get good sleep,
And keep your to-do list short, not steep.

question: How do I make a cup of tea?
poem:
Boil some fresh water and pour it hot,
Over a tea bag in a cup or a pot;
Let it steep for three to five minutes or so,
Then add milk or lemon, and off you go.

question: What is the largest ocean?
poem:
The Pacific Ocean is the largest by far,
It stretches from Asia to where the Americas are;
It covers about a third of Earth's face,
And holds the deepest trench in any place.

question: Who invented the telephone?
poem:
Alexander Graham Bell is the name we recall,
He patented the telephone for one and all;
In eighteen seventy-six it first rang,
And soon across cities its ringing sang.

question: Why do birds migrate?
poem:
When winter brings cold and the food grows thin,
Many birds fly south, where warmer days begin;
They travel to places with food to eat,
Then return in spring for their nests and the heat.

question: What causes earthquakes?
poem:
Earth's crust is made of plates that slowly slide,
They push and they pull from side to side;
When stress builds up and the rocks break free,
The ground starts to shake for all to see.

question: What is DNA?
poem:
DNA is the code inside each cell,
It holds the instructions your body knows well;
Shaped like a twisted ladder, a double helix shape,
It carries traits from your parents you cannot escape.

question: Why is exercise important?
poem:
Exercise keeps your heart and muscles strong,
It helps you stay healthy all life long;
It lifts your mood and helps you sleep,
And builds up energy that you can keep.

question: What language is spoken in Brazil?
poem:
In Brazil, people speak Portuguese every day,
A language that came from Portugal far away;
Explorers from Portugal arrived long ago,
So the language they brought is the one people know.

question: How many bones are in the human body?
poem:
An adult's skeleton holds two hundred six bones,
They protect your organs like sturdy stones;
A baby is born with nearly three hundred in all,
But some fuse together as children grow tall.

question: What is the speed of light?
poem:
Light moves at about three hundred thousand kilometers each second,
It is the fastest speed, scientists have reckoned;
From the Sun, its light takes eight minutes to arrive,
To warm up our planet and keep life alive.

question: Why do onions make you cry?
poem:
When you cut an onion, it releases a gas,
That floats to your eyes as the moments pass;
Your eyes sting and water to wash it away,
So chill it or use a sharp knife to save the day.

question: What is inflation?
poem:
Inflation means prices go up over time,
So a coin buys less than it did in its prime;
Your money is worth less when the costs climb high,
And the same weekly shopping costs more to buy.

question: How does a rainbow form?
poem:
When sunlight shines through raindrops in the air,
The light bends and splits into colors there;
Red, orange, yellow, green, blue, and more,
Spread in an arc, a sight to adore.

question: Who was Marie Curie?
poem:
Marie Curie was a scientist bright,
Who studied radiation and its hidden might;
She was the first woman to win a Nobel Prize,
And won it twice, to the whole world's surprise.

question: What is the capital of Japan?
poem:
Tokyo is the capital of Japan,
A huge, busy city with a modern plan;
Its neon streets and old temples combine,
With bullet trains running in a speedy line.

question: How do airplanes fly?
poem:
The wings of a plane are shaped to make lift,
As air flows around them, fast and swift;
The engines push forward to give it speed,
When lift beats the weight, up it goes indeed.

question: What is the smallest planet in our solar system?
poem:
Mercury is the smallest planet we know,
The closest to the Sun, racing to and fro;
Its days are scorching, its nights freezing cold,
Its surface is cratered, gray, and very old.

question: Why do we have day and night?
poem:
The Earth spins around once every day,
So half faces the Sun and gets its bright ray;
The other half turns to the dark of space,
And night falls there until morning's embrace.

question: How do fish breathe underwater?
poem:
Fish breathe through gills on each side of their head,
They take in water instead of air, it is said;
The gills pull out the oxygen hidden inside,
Then let the water flow out the other side.

question: What is the longest river in the world?
poem:
The Nile is often named the longest of all,
Though the Amazon's backers make a strong call;
Both stretch well over six thousand kilometers long,
And measuring rivers can easily go wrong.

question: What is the capital of Australia?
poem:
Many think Sydney, but that is not right,
The capital is Canberra, a planned city site;
It was built as a compromise in its day,
Between rival Sydney and Melbourne, they say.

question: How do I boil an egg?
poem:
Place eggs in a pot and bring water to boil,
Then simmer them gently, no stirring, no toil;
Cook six minutes for soft, ten for a firm bite,
Then cool them in ice so the shells peel off right.

question: How does the Sun produce energy?
poem:
Deep in the Sun's core, the pressure is great,
Hydrogen atoms fuse at a fast rate;
They turn into helium and release light and heat,
Which reaches our planet, making life complete.

question: What is a volcano?
poem:
A volcano is an opening in Earth's crust,
Where melted rock rises up when it must;
Lava, ash, and gases burst into the air,
And build up a mountain over years with care.

question: What is democracy?
poem:
Democracy means that the people decide,
Through free elections, they choose who will guide;
Everyone's voice can be heard in a vote,
And rights like free speech are things to note.

question: Who discovered penicillin?
poem:
Alexander Fleming, in nineteen twenty-eight,
Saw mold kill bacteria on a culture plate;
Called penicillin, it saved many a life,
Fighting infections that caused pain and strife.

question: How do magnets work?
poem:
Magnets pull iron with an unseen force,
That comes from electrons' spin, of course;
Opposite poles pull close like a friend,
But matching poles push apart in the end.

question: How can I stay focused while studying?
poem:
Put your phone away and find a quiet space,
Set a clear goal and work at a steady pace;
Take a short break after each half hour,
And drink some water to keep up your power.

question: What is a leap year?
poem:
A leap year adds one extra day,
To keep our calendar from drifting away;
February gets twenty-nine days instead,
Almost every four years, as the rules have said.

question: Why do we have fingerprints?
poem:
Our fingertips have ridges that help us grip,
So objects are less likely to slip;
They may help us feel textures in more detail,
And each pattern is unique, without fail.

question: What is the Great Wall of China?
poem:
The Great Wall of China is long and old,
Built over centuries, as stories have told;
Soldiers kept watch from its towers on guard,
Against raids from the north, it stood tall and hard.

question: How does recycling help the planet?
poem:
Recycling turns old things into new,
So we use fewer trees and mine less too;
It keeps waste out of landfills and seas,
And saves lots of energy with ease.

question: What is the freezing point of water?
poem:
Pure water becomes ice at zero degrees,
In Celsius, the scale most of the world sees;
In Fahrenheit, that is thirty-two,
And salt makes it freeze lower, it is true.

question: Why do dogs wag their tails?
poem:
Dogs wag their tails to show how they feel,
A message to others, both clear and real;
A loose, happy wag often means they are glad,
But a stiff one may warn they are nervous or mad.

question: What is the speed of sound?
poem:
In air, sound travels at a good speed,
Three hundred forty meters a second, indeed;
It moves even faster through water and steel,
But it cannot cross space, where silence is real.

question: What is the human brain made of?
poem:
Your brain has billions of neurons inside,
Tiny nerve cells that send signals far and wide;
They link through connections that chat all day,
Controlling your thoughts and the way you play.

question: How do I write a good email?
poem:
Start with a subject that is short and clear,
Then greet the reader so the tone is sincere;
Keep your message brief and polite all the way,
And end with thanks and the next step today.

question: Why can we see the Moon during the day?
poem:
The Moon is lit by the Sun's bright rays,
And it is often above us on many days;
Since it is bright and close to our view,
We can spot it in daytime against the blue.

question: What is climate change?
poem:
Our planet keeps warming as the years go by,
As gases from burning fuels trap heat in the sky;
This melts the ice and raises the seas,
And brings heat waves, floods, and dying trees.

question: How do I make friends in a new city?
poem:
Join a club or a class that you like,
Like cooking, a sport, or a weekend hike;
Say yes to invites and talk to new faces,
And meet up again in your favorite places.

question: What is artificial intelligence?
poem:
Artificial intelligence means machines that learn,
From lots of examples, with each new turn;
They spot patterns in data to help them decide,
Like translating words or acting as a guide.

question: What is the largest animal on Earth?
poem:
The blue whale is the largest of any creature,
Its massive size is its most famous feature;
It can grow to thirty meters from head to tail,
And eats tiny krill by the ton, without fail.

question: What is the difference between weather and climate?
poem:
Weather is what happens outside today,
The rain or the sun that comes our way;
Climate is the pattern a region knows,
Measured over decades as the weather goes.

question: How does a computer store information?
poem:
Computers keep data as zeros and ones,
In tiny switches through which current runs;
Groups of these bits make photos and text,
And files you can open from one day to the next.

question: Why do we have tides?
poem:
The Moon's gravity pulls on the sea,
Making the water bulge, as you can see;
As Earth spins, coasts pass through these bulges each day,
So tides rise and fall in a regular way.

question: What is the capital of Canada?
poem:
Ottawa is Canada's capital city,
Not Toronto, though Toronto is large and pretty;
It sits by a river in Ontario's land,
Where Parliament Hill stands proud and grand.

question: Why should I wear sunscreen?
poem:
Sunscreen protects from the Sun's UV rays,
That can burn your skin on bright, sunny days;
Too much sun over years can lead to skin cancer,
So wearing protection is the smart answer.

question: What is a rainforest?
poem:
Rainforests are warm with rain almost every day,
With tall trees where countless creatures stay;
They shelter over half of all species on land,
And help clean the air, as experts understand.

question: How can I save energy at home?
poem:
Switch off the lights when you leave a room,
And unplug the chargers that idly consume;
Wear a warm sweater instead of more heat,
And wash clothes cooler to make savings complete.

question: What is the Big Bang?
poem:
The Big Bang is the start of all that we know,
About thirteen point eight billion years ago;
Everything began very hot and small,
Then expanded and cooled to form stars and all.

question: Who was Albert Einstein?
poem:
Albert Einstein was a physicist great,
Whose theory of relativity changed science's fate;
He showed that mass and energy are tied,
With E equals mc squared as his guide.

question: Why are carrots good for you?
poem:
Carrots contain a lot of vitamin A,
Which helps your eyes see in dim light each day;
They are full of fiber that helps you digest,
A crunchy snack that is one of the best.

question: What is a star?
poem:
A star is a ball of glowing gas,
That shines in the sky as the ages pass;
Our Sun is the star that is closest by,
The others are farther, so they look small in the sky.

question: How can I learn a new language?
poem:
Practice a little every single day,
With apps, books, or songs that you like to play;
Speak with native speakers whenever you can,
And don't fear mistakes, they are part of the plan.

question: What is the capital of Italy?
poem:
The capital of Italy is Rome,
Where ancient ruins and churches make their home;
The Colosseum stands from a time long ago,
And the Vatican lies within it, as many know.

question: What is the stock market?
poem:
The stock market is where shares are sold,
Small pieces of companies that people hold;
When a business grows, its shares may rise,
But prices can fall, so invest with wise eyes.

question: How do submarines dive?
poem:
Submarines take in water to make them weigh more,
So they sink beneath waves toward the ocean floor;
To rise again, they push water out with air,
And float back up to the surface from there.

question: Why do stars twinkle?
poem:
Stars twinkle because of the air in between,
Its moving layers bend the light that is seen;
The light shifts and wobbles as it travels through,
So stars seem to sparkle in the night's deep blue.

question: What is the capital of Germany?
poem:
The capital of Germany is Berlin,
A city where history and art are woven in;
Its famous wall divided it in two,
Until it fell in nineteen eighty-nine, it's true.

question: What is the flu?
poem:
The flu is caused by a virus that spreads,
And can send many people straight to their beds;
A yearly vaccine can help you stay well,
And washing your hands also helps, as doctors tell.

question: What is a carbon footprint?
poem:
A carbon footprint counts the gases you make,
From the trips that you drive to the meals that you bake;
Flying less and saving power make it shrink,
More than most people might expect or think.

question: How do I care for a houseplant?
poem:
Give your plant water when the soil feels dry,
And find it a spot where the light comes by;
Too much water makes the roots slowly rot,
So drain any water left in the pot.

question: What are the Olympic Games?
poem:
The Olympics are games held every four years,
Where athletes compete to the crowd's loud cheers;
They began long ago in ancient Greece,
And now bring nations together in peace.

question: Why do apples turn brown when cut?
poem:
When you cut an apple, its cells break apart,
And oxygen in the air gets a start;
An enzyme reacts and turns the flesh brown,
Lemon juice slows it and keeps the color down.

question: What is a hurricane?
poem:
A hurricane is a huge, spinning storm,
That forms over oceans where waters are warm;
Its winds can be strong enough to knock out power,
Blowing over one hundred nineteen kilometers an hour.

question: How do I prepare for a job interview?
poem:
Learn about the company before you go,
And think of examples of skills you can show;
Practice your answers out loud with a friend,
And bring a few questions to ask at the end.

question: Who built the pyramids of Egypt?
poem:
The ancient Egyptians built them long ago,
As tombs for their kings, so the records show;
Thousands of skilled workers moved stones by hand,
Across the hot desert, a feat truly grand.

question: What is the largest organ of the human body?
poem:
Your skin is the largest organ of all,
It wraps you from head to toe like a wall;
It keeps out germs and holds water in,
And helps you feel touch through the nerves in your skin.

question: What was the Renaissance?
poem:
The Renaissance was a time of rebirth,
When learning and art showed their new worth;
It began in Italy six hundred years ago,
With artists like Leonardo putting on a show.

question: Why do we pay taxes?
poem:
Taxes are money we pay to the state,
To fund what we share, both small and great;
Like schools, roads, hospitals, and police,
Which help keep our towns running in peace.

question: How do clouds form?
poem:
The Sun warms the water, which rises up high,
Then cools into droplets up in the sky;
These droplets gather on dust in the air,
And form the white clouds that float up there.

question: What is a mammal?
poem:
A mammal has hair or fur on its skin,
And feeds its young milk to help them begin;
Most give birth to live babies, not eggs, it is true,
Like dogs, whales, and humans, and bats and cows too.
